summary: PRIVATE-RISK LAST LOOK (local files only, 0 Kaggle calls, no model re-run). The default pair is P3 {V_pub = exp87a (K + CI, 0.959), #37}. Write c+k for the private effect of cap 6 + K and i for CI, with #37 = 0. Then P3 = max(c+k+i, 0), P2 {exp87a, exp75} = max(c+k+i, i), and the card's info row {exp85a, exp75} = max(c+k, i). P3 does clearly worse only in the two mixed quadrants. (1) CI negative, cap+K positive: p ~0.30; loses to {exp85a, exp75} by min(|i|, c+k) ~0.0003-0.0008. (2) cap+K negative, CI positive: p ~0.12; loses to P2 by min(i, |c+k|). Both are small, roughly 10-30 ranks: there are ~30 teams per 0.001 in the 0.957-0.959 blocks. mc26 already models both, and card v5 already shows both (P2 as a trade, the split pair as an out-of-plan info row). The other scenarios are the exp89r >= 0.960 SEC/DIS winner's curse (~0.12 joint), K failing on private (the Cyrus case, ~0.06-0.15), insertion failing (~0.03-0.05 that #38 would matter), and an exp89p 0.959 k = 0 tie (~0.12). Each is either already covered by the structure or can only be hedged post-hoc against a refuted idea (I-532, I-444). No pre-registered rule should change before the reads. NEW FACT: at 02:14Z the public bronze line (rank ~398) is inside the 0.955 block (321-431) and silver (~199) is inside the 0.957 block (157-205). mc26 was fitted when bronze sat in the 0.954 block, so #37 (0.954; 0.954 block = 432-567) is now 34-169 ranks BELOW the public bronze line. Card v5 has no medal-line field. One text-only card info line is proposed for the 12:03Z fill. Nothing reaches R8: no new inference or post-processing idea.

At 02:14Z (3,979 teams) bronze (top 10% ~ rank 398) falls inside the 0.955 block (111 teams, ranks 321-431) and silver (~199) inside the 0.957 block (49 teams, 157-205). mc26's field (LB 13:18Z 28 Sep) had bronze = rank 396 in the 0.954 block (349-488) and silver in the 0.956 block. Since then: 0.956 68 -> 115, 0.955 97 -> 111, 0.957 42 -> 49. Consequences: #37 (0.954; the 0.954 block is now 432-567) sits 34-169 ranks below the public bronze line, and so would exp75 at 0.954; exp75 at 0.955 would straddle the line. exp87a 0.959 is rank 132 (silver margin ~0.002 display, bronze margin ~0.004). The partner's medal value therefore now comes almost entirely from worlds where the 0.955-0.957 mass falls on private, i.e. a shared public-selected lever such as K fails. This does not change the partner ranking in rule v2: a partner with a higher public score (exp75 >= 0.955) gains slightly, which is already the rule-v2 (a)/(b) direction. Card v5 (sha8 aab8801a) has no medal-line field (grep for medal-line words = 0 hits in the card body), and its model text says only that it was not recomputed for another V_pub, not that the field moved.

findings.what: PRIVATE SCENARIO TABLE for the recommended pair P3 {exp87a, #37}: the cases where it does clearly worse than an alternative, with rough probabilities. The priors are mc26-like: K ~N(+0.0009, 0.0012); cap 6 ~N(+0.0005, 0.0012) (public +0.002, lab -0.0006); CI P(>0) ~0.6. That gives P(c+k < 0) ~0.2. S1 (p ~0.30): CI < 0 on private while cap 6 + K > 0. P3 loses to the out-of-plan {exp85a 56629533, exp75} by min(|i|, c+k), ~0.0003-0.0008 (~10-25 ranks). This is mc26 RESULT 2 ({exp85a, exp75} ahead on bronze in all 12 runs), and the card already shows it as an info row that needs the user's separate yes. S2 (p ~0.12): cap 6 + K < 0 while CI > 0. P3 loses to P2 {exp87a, exp75} by min(i, |c+k|). Rule v2 (b) shows P2 as a trade at exp75 >= 0.955. S3 (p ~0.25 x ~0.5 = ~0.12): exp89r reads >= 0.960 and becomes V_pub, but its +0.001 over exp87a is SEC/DIS public noise. SEC has a negative dummy-lab prior and 0 of 5 secondary swaps held on the LB. {exp89r, #37} then trails {exp87a, #37} by ~0.0005-0.002. The only hedge breaks the max-display rule, which is +EV in 5 of 6 cells (I-532, refuted). S4 (p ~0.06-0.15): K fails on private (the Cyrus 743929 case). The ~275 teams at 0.955-0.957 that likely carry JT's K fall with us, so V_pub keeps most of its relative rank, and a no-K partner (#37 / exp75) climbs. The agreed structure already covers this; the rejected JT pair {exp87a, exp85a} / {exp87a, exp79a} would not. S5 (p ~0.03-0.05): the K2 insertion base itself is negative on private by more than V_pub's 0.006 public lead, so the twin #38 would be the better partner. The loss is ~0.0005 and both files are below bronze either way, so it has no medal value. S6 (p ~0.3 x ~0.4 = ~0.12): exp89p reads 0.959 with k = 0. The 02:02Z conservative running-champion reading keeps exp87a (CI) over exp89p (non-CI, SEC). If CI < SEC on private, that costs ~0.0005. It is pre-registered, and CI has two LB '+' reads against SEC's negative lab prior. S7 (~0): a private-only runtime or stage failure; there is one hidden run, bounded per I-539. VERDICT: no scenario is both likely (>= ~0.3) and cheap to hedge without either a post-hoc change to a logged rule or a structure the user already declined. S1 is the most likely, but its hedge moves V_pub out of the pair, and the card already offers that to the user.
